title: Territory Map, Fourth Revision
text: Aides present a peace framework with a map. The lines have been redrawn so often that the paper is now mostly marker.

options.label: Study the map
options.result: You studied the borders for an hour. Nobody can tell you which line is current, but you nodded at all of them.

ignore.text: The map went unread. A fifth revision arrived anyway, with a new color of marker.

inspiredBy: Reports in late 2025 of a rapidly revised multi-point Ukraine peace framework.

title: Strait Shipping Lanes
text: A navy analyst explains a narrow waterway, its tolls and who may sail through it. You are asked to hold the pointer.

options.label: Follow the lanes
options.result: You learned that the strait is narrow, important and not available for naming rights.

ignore.text: The shipping brief was skipped. Tankers waited in a long, patient line for guidance.

inspiredBy: Spring 2026 talks with Iran about reopening the Strait of Hormuz and banning tolls.

title: Rare Earths for Beginners
text: A trade official walks you through magnets, mining and export controls. The word "rare" is used to hold your interest.

options.label: Take notes
options.result: You now understand why a one-year pause on export controls counts as a breakthrough. Your notes say "magnets: big."

ignore.text: The primer went unread. The truce's expiry date moved closer without comment.

inspiredBy: The October 2025 Busan summit truce pausing China's rare earth export controls for a year.

title: Who Runs What, Now
text: A thick binder explains the transition, the oil contracts and who answers the phones. Slide four is titled "We are running it."

options.label: Read the binder
options.result: You learned that "running" a country involves paperwork, and that nobody has found the stapler.

ignore.text: The binder stayed shut. The transition plan was cited by three people who had also not read it.

inspiredBy: January 2026 statements that the US would "run" Venezuela during a transition.

title: Phase Two Flowchart
text: A diplomat unrolls a flowchart of ceasefire phases, boards and technocratic committees. Your name appears on the first box and is circled twice.

options.label: Trace the arrows
options.result: You followed every arrow. Several lead back to a box marked "to be determined," which you declined to rename.

ignore.text: The flowchart was folded away. Phase two continued to be described as "imminent."

inspiredBy: The 2025 to 2026 phased Gaza ceasefire plan and its oversight board.

title: Pyongyang Reading Pack
text: An analyst offers a dossier on a reclusive nuclear state. It is mostly text. The photo of you shaking hands is on page ninety.

options.label: Read to page ninety
options.result: You read the whole dossier and found the handshake photo. You also learned things about missiles, which was not the plan.

ignore.text: The dossier went unopened. It was filed under "future summit, possibly."

inspiredBy: Early 2026 remarks that Trump expects to meet North Korea's leader again.

title: Legal Memo on Authorizations
text: Counsel delivers a memo on what Congress must approve and what it merely needs to be told about. It uses the phrase "notwithstanding" eleven times.

options.label: Read all of it
options.result: You read the memo. It concludes that the Senate would like to be asked first, which you found surprising.

ignore.text: The memo went unread. A war powers resolution advanced, and nobody had prepared a comment.

inspiredBy: January 2026 Senate war powers votes after the operation in Venezuela.

title: New Stationery Order
text: The Pentagon has a new secondary name, and a printing contractor needs a decision on letterhead, signs and seventeen thousand lanyards.

options.label: Ask Congress, as the law requires
options.result: Congress has been asked. Several hearings are scheduled. The lanyards remain blank, which is the most accurate thing printed so far.

options.label: Print it in gold, order double
options.result: The lanyards say WAR in gold foil. Half the staff adopted them with enthusiasm. The other half asked about the law.

ignore.text: The stationery order stalled. Two rival signs now hang above the same door.

inspiredBy: The September 2025 order styling the Defense Department as the Department of War.

title: Summit Seating Chart
text: Protocol needs an arrangement for the Alaska meeting. The red carpet is cleared, the bomber flyover is booked and the table question is open.

options.label: Standard table, standard agenda
options.result: A normal table was set with a normal agenda. The flyover was canceled. The briefing staff nearly wept with relief.

options.label: Longer carpet, louder flyover
options.result: The carpet now reaches the horizon. Both delegations arrived to applause and left without a deal, but with very good photos.

ignore.text: The seating chart was never approved. Both delegations arrived and lined up politely for the same chair.

inspiredBy: The August 2025 Alaska summit with a red carpet welcome and military flyover.

title: Board Charter, Article One
text: Lawyers draft the charter for a new international peace board. Article one lists the chair as you, with a blank line for the end date.

options.label: Add a term limit
options.result: The chair now serves a fixed term. Several member states relaxed visibly, and the gavel was taken away for polishing.

options.label: Leave the blank line blank
options.result: The line stays blank. Members noticed that the gavel is larger than the other chairs' gavels. There are no other gavels.

ignore.text: The charter went unsigned. The board met anyway and elected an empty chair, then argued about whose it was.

inspiredBy: January 2026 launch of Trump's Board of Peace for Gaza, with Trump as chair.

title: Trophy Shelf Allocation
text: A soccer federation has presented a peace trophy, and the Oval Office is short on shelf space. Staff want a ruling on where it goes.

options.label: Put it in a display case
options.result: The trophy sits in a modest case in a hallway. It was described as "not a Nobel" by a staffer, quietly, in a closet.

options.label: Clear the mantel for it
options.result: The trophy now holds the mantel, lit from three angles. A reporter asked if it was the Nobel. You did not answer the question.

ignore.text: The trophy sat in a box beside the desk. The box got a nameplate.

inspiredBy: December 2025, when FIFA's president presented Trump with an inaugural peace prize.

title: What to Call the Deal
text: Negotiators have a draft agreement with a neutral title. A speechwriter proposes that it carry your name, in the interest of clarity.

options.label: Keep the neutral title
options.result: The agreement kept its plain title. Both sides signed quickly, mostly in relief that nobody would need to say your name in a toast.

options.label: Call it the Trump Accord
options.result: The title is now your name. The other party asked for a footnote with a different name. The footnote is larger than the agreement.

ignore.text: The deal had no name by deadline. Three nicknames circulated, all of them yours.

inspiredBy: Peace agreements in 2025 that Trump announced as his own achievements.

title: Choice of Signing Pen
text: A regional leader will host a peace signing. Protocol offers a plain pen, or a ceremonial one three feet long that must be held with both hands.

options.label: Use the plain pen
options.result: The ceremony ran on time. The giant pen was passed to a museum, where it remains the largest object in the case.

options.label: Take the three-foot pen
options.result: Your signature covered two pages and a table. Cameras loved it. The other signatories needed a stepladder to reach the line.

ignore.text: The pen question was left open. The signing started late while two aides argued over a ballpoint.

inspiredBy: The October 2025 Gaza peace summit and signing ceremony in Egypt.

title: Class of Battleship
text: Naval planners need a name for a proposed new warship class. Their working title is "Trump-class," in gold, with a statue on the bow.

options.label: Send it to a naming committee
options.result: The committee is now working on it. The navy was delighted, mostly because committees take years and budgets take longer.

options.label: Approve Trump-class
options.result: The class is named. Sailors report that the gold paint is hard to keep from chipping. A tug is being renamed in solidarity.

ignore.text: The naming request lapsed. The warships stayed unnamed, and one was called Hull Number Four.

inspiredBy: December 2025 announcement of a planned "Trump-class" battleship fleet.

title: Missile Shield Branding
text: A defense contractor presents a missile shield concept. Engineers want to talk costs. Marketing wants to talk about the golden dome and the logo.

options.label: Review the cost estimates
options.result: The cost estimates were reviewed. They had several more zeros than the logo, which was returned for gold edges.

options.label: Approve the logo first
options.result: The logo was approved in four minutes. The cost review is scheduled after the unveiling, which will be held under an actual gold dome.

ignore.text: The shield proposal stalled. The contractor sent a larger logo as a reminder.

inspiredBy: The 2025 Golden Dome missile defense initiative announced by the administration.

title: All Generals, One Room, Short Notice
text: The defense secretary proposes to summon every general and admiral to a single base for a speech. Travel costs are already a rounding error to someone.

options.label: Do it by video link
options.result: Generals logged in from forty time zones. The connection dropped during the applause, which was statistically the most honest part.

options.label: Fill the hall, bring flags
options.result: The hall was full, silent and very tall. Nobody clapped until a staffer clapped first, which was noted by several people for the record.

ignore.text: The speech was never scheduled. The generals stayed at their posts, vaguely uneasy about why.

inspiredBy: The September 30, 2025 address to hundreds of generals and admirals at Quantico.

title: How Many Wars Did You Settle
text: A reporter asks you to list the wars you have settled. You have been saying eight. Staff have a laminated list and it is not unanimous.

options.label: Read the laminated list
options.result: You read out the list. Several items were described by the other parties as "a pause." You thanked them for the clarification.

options.label: "Eight. Maybe nine. Ask me again"
options.result: The number rose by one while the reporter was asking a follow-up. Aides added a ninth line in pencil and hoped no one would ask which.

ignore.text: You skipped the question. The count was announced on your behalf, in a font that kept growing.

inspiredBy: 2025 to 2026 repeated claims that Trump had "settled eight wars."

title: The Two-Week Timeline
text: A reporter asks when you will decide on the next step in a long negotiation. Your usual answer is "two weeks." They have started a countdown clock.

options.label: Give a real date
options.result: You gave a date. Calendars were checked. Everyone looked at the date as if it might bite.

options.label: "Two weeks. Maybe less"
options.result: The clock restarted. Reporters noted that it has restarted before. You said the clock is also a very good clock.

ignore.text: You skipped the question. The countdown clock got a sponsor.

inspiredBy: Recurring 2025 "two weeks" deadlines Trump set for Russia and Iran decisions.

title: Post-Summit Press Conference
text: A summit ended with warm handshakes and no agreement. Reporters are waiting to ask what, precisely, was achieved.

options.label: Admit there is no deal yet
options.result: "No deal until there's a deal," you said. It was a clean sentence and nobody could find anything wrong with it, which unsettled the room.

options.label: Call it a 10 out of 10
options.result: You scored the summit a ten. The foreign press asked who the judges were. You said you were all of them.

ignore.text: You left without questions. The summit was reviewed by everyone but you.

inspiredBy: The August 2025 Alaska summit press remarks, "there's no deal until there's a deal."

title: The Predecessor Comparison
text: A reporter wonders if you still think the Nobel committee treats you unfairly compared with a predecessor who won early.

options.label: Say the process is theirs
options.result: You said the committee decides for itself. You said it in a voice that suggested you were reading someone else's note.

options.label: "He got it in ten seconds"
options.result: You gave a timed comparison. The stopwatch you borrowed from a reporter is now in your pocket.

ignore.text: You dodged the question. A late-night host answered it, with a stopwatch.

inspiredBy: 2025 remarks that Trump would have won the Nobel "in ten seconds" if named Obama.

title: The Nobel Announcement
text: The prize was announced and went to someone else. Reporters want a reaction, and the Oval Office has been ready with a statement since August.

options.label: Congratulate the winner
options.result: You offered warm words for the winner. Aides filed the August statement under "contingency, extremely detailed."

options.label: Blame the committee's country
options.result: You pointed at a small, cold country. Its prime minister said, politely and twice, that she does not run the committee.

ignore.text: You skipped the announcement. The medal went to someone else, and the August statement was quietly sent anyway.

inspiredBy: October 2025, when the Nobel Peace Prize went to another laureate and Trump complained.

title: Will You Meet Him Again
text: Asked about another meeting with a reclusive leader, you say you expect one. His sister's office says no messages were ever exchanged.

options.label: "No date yet"
options.result: You said nothing had been scheduled. A diplomat nearby stopped holding her breath, then resumed when you smiled.

options.label: "We get along. Great relationship"
options.result: You described the relationship in glowing terms. The other side described it in none. Both statements were filed for the museum.

ignore.text: You skipped the question. Several analysts began guessing at the venue, mostly golf clubs.

inspiredBy: Early 2026 comments that Trump expects to meet Kim Jong Un and a denial from Pyongyang.

title: The Two-Hour Call
text: A rival president wants to talk for as long as it takes. Two hours later, the plan is to talk again and to describe the call as "excellent."

options.label: Keep it to thirty minutes
options.result: You hung up on time. Your counterpart noted that your schedule was tighter than his, and that was his whole message.

options.label: Stay on, order lunch
options.result: The call ran past lunch, dinner and two allied phone calls waiting in line. The word "excellent" was used eleven times.

ignore.text: You missed the call. A statement said it went very well, anyway.

inspiredBy: May 2025, when Trump and Putin spoke for over two hours without a ceasefire deal.

title: A President Wants Guarantees
text: Ukraine's president calls to ask for security guarantees, in writing, on official paper. He suggests wording and a jacket.

options.label: Agree to review a draft
options.result: You asked for the draft. The draft arrived with eleven names for the guarantees and none of them were yours.

options.label: Ask about the jacket instead
options.result: You asked about the jacket for a long time. The president admitted the jacket was not on the agenda and noted that nothing else was.

ignore.text: You didn't return the call. A European leader called three times to make up for it, at length.

inspiredBy: Late 2025 meetings between Trump and Ukraine's president over security guarantees.

title: A Call From Beijing
text: China's president phones about the trade truce. He is pleased with it and would like the expiry date to be, ideally, someday.

options.label: Agree to extend the truce
options.result: The truce got another two months. Both leaders called it a great friendship, and both aides checked the calendar again.

options.label: Propose a bigger deal, bigger pens
options.result: You proposed a historic agreement with unusually large pens. The call ended with polite interest and a very short note.

ignore.text: You missed the call. The truce's expiry date was quietly circled in red by someone.

inspiredBy: The Busan truce of October 2025 and later extension talks with China's president.

title: Norway Would Like to Clarify
text: Norway's prime minister calls to explain, again, that the Nobel committee is independent and that she cannot award you anything.

options.label: Thank her for clarifying
options.result: You thanked her. She seemed relieved the call went well, and you did not mention the medal for four whole minutes.

options.label: Ask if she can "make a call"
options.result: You asked her to make a call to Oslo. She said that she was in Oslo. You asked again, more slowly.

ignore.text: You skipped the call. Norway's explanation was published, and it was a little longer than before.

inspiredBy: October 2025, when Norway's prime minister said the Nobel Committee is independent of government.

title: The Mediator Calls In
text: A mediating country's leader calls with progress on talks. He also mentions, in passing, that he has put your name forward for an award.

options.label: Focus on the talks
options.result: You asked about the talks first. The mediator reported steady progress, a preliminary text and some very nice tea.

options.label: Ask about the award first
options.result: You asked about the award for ten minutes. The talks were described as "still alive," which someone wrote down.

ignore.text: You missed the call. The mediator sent a text, and a second one, politely asking about the first.

inspiredBy: 2025 nominations of Trump for the Nobel by several governments, and mediation in Iran talks in 2026.

title: An Ally Calls About Membership
text: An allied prime minister is unhappy that your new peace board was not coordinated with him. He is also, reluctantly, going to join it.

options.label: Offer a say in the agenda
options.result: He got a seat and a say. The agenda is now seven pages long, and your own agenda item is on page one.

options.label: Remind him who chairs it
options.result: You reminded him who chairs it, twice. He joined anyway, warmly, in the tone of a man signing an electric bill.

ignore.text: You left the call unanswered. A second ally was told to wait, and joined the waiting.

inspiredBy: January 2026 reports that Israel first criticized, then joined, the Board of Peace.

title: A Gift Medal From a Laureate
text: A Nobel laureate from a country you recently handled offers to give you her medal. A lawyer recalls that the prize cannot be transferred.

options.label: Accept it as a keepsake
options.result: You took it as a thank-you gift. A committee noted the prize remains hers, and you said you knew that, mostly.

options.label: Announce you now hold the prize
options.result: You said the prize is now yours. Oslo replied that a medal and a prize are different things, in a very short press release.

ignore.text: You didn't take the call. The medal went to a box labeled "sensitive," beside an unmarked second box.

inspiredBy: January 2026, when Venezuela's opposition leader gave Trump her Nobel medal.

title: The Envoy Reports From Moscow
text: Your envoy calls after a long meeting with a rival president. He is thrilled. He cannot say exactly what was agreed, only that tea was involved.

options.label: Ask for the notes in writing
options.result: The envoy promised written notes. They arrived with six pages of tea and one of substance, which you declared a good ratio.

options.label: "Tell the press it's close"
options.result: "Closer than ever," you told the press. The other side called a press conference to say it was also standing in the same place.

ignore.text: You didn't take the call. The envoy briefed the wrong person, who was thrilled too.

inspiredBy: December 2025 meetings between a US envoy and Russia's president on a new peace proposal.

title: Three Chairs in Shenzhen
text: The summit hosts propose a first three-way meeting with the leaders of China and Russia. Staff ask what you plan to say. You ask how big the table is.

options.label: Go in with a written agenda
options.result: Eleven agenda items, and you reached nine. Both leaders looked faintly disappointed, which staff count as a success.

options.label: Wing it and call it the Big Three
options.result: You named it the Big Three and gave yourself the middle chair. Allies watched the photo with the sound off.

ignore.text: No answer was sent. The other two met anyway and saved you a chair, near the door.

inspiredBy: November 2026: the White House announced a first trilateral meeting of Trump, Putin and Xi around the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
